Plainva follows a strict rule: **every file it writes must still open in Obsidian.** Notes are standard Markdown + YAML frontmatter; Plainva-specific presentation lives under a single namespaced `plainva:` key that other tools simply ignore. Existing vaults are never migrated or reformatted. The optional OKF conventions (typed notes, managed `index.md` files) are opt-in.

Note that the guarantee runs one way: Obsidian can always **open** what Plainva writes, but once a vault uses Plainva features (`.base` extensions such as boards or relations, managed `index.md` files), **editing** those specific files in Obsidian can break that functionality — Obsidian does not know the `plainva:` extensions. Notes without Plainva extensions can be edited anywhere, anytime. Details in the FAQ.

Plainva has no code-plugin sandbox — the vault *is* the interface. Every file is plain Markdown or YAML with an open, documented format, so any script, CLI tool or AI agent can read and write your vault directly and safely, with no Plainva-specific API to learn. See the guide's Automation & Scripts page and the machine-oriented file format reference; for AI agents there is a ready-made `AGENTS.md` template and skill. AI apps on the same computer (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, editors) can also read the vault through Plainva's read-only MCP server — no network port, folders granted per app — see Connecting AI apps. A direct write skips Plainva's pre-write backup — the version history only holds what Plainva wrote — so larger agent edits belong in a vault under Git. (A dedicated in-app plugin system remains a separate post-1.0 idea.)

|📝 Web form|Fills corporate application forms in a **separate dedicated browser**: type a URL to open it in a new tab and manage the URL history without clobbering pages you already have open; each page can be switched between batch and point-and-fill. It reads the whole page and checks each value before filling, or confirms a suggestion next to the input you click; fields the rules cannot recognise can be handed to the AI, which **only receives page text and field names, never your Profile values**. The browser model is shared with the apply desk but runs in its own window; fill records contain real values and stay local. **It fills, it never submits**, and passwords and verification codes are never filled automatically; **it only writes into text-like controls** — dropdowns, radio buttons, checkboxes and date pickers are left alone and honestly listed as “needs your click”; a separate **relaxed mode** can try label and context matching and click dropdown and popover options (see the next row). When filling finishes it shows the **success rate** (fields filled / readable fields on the page) and can export **redacted diagnostics that contain no Resume values**, which makes it easy to report a field it could not recognise|

|🟢 Relaxed mode|The Web form's **optional exception, off by default**: once you explicitly switch it on, it tries to match unrecognised text inputs (including Custom Fields) by label and context and clicks dropdown and popover options itself (**strict option matching plus read-back verification**); in relaxed text matching, low-confidence candidates backed only by weak context are left unticked for you to confirm, and repeated experience entries are only filled when the record count and the page order can be paired. Consent and declaration checkboxes still need item-by-item confirmation; date pickers and file uploads are never touched. The Job assistant has no tool to switch it on — do it on the page or in Settings. Relaxed matching can pick wrong, so proofread after filling; a multi-value popover only acts when every value matches|

|🧠 Learnt while filling|When you hit a field **ResumeForge does not know**, **both entry points** can record it: batch mode shows one summary prompt when it finishes (**everything ticked, everything “General” by default**, and you can untick individual items), and point-and-fill puts a “Remember this” next to **every box**, so you can **record it on the spot** — **even a box it recognised but has no value for** (fill it in place without jumping to another page). Once remembered, the same field is **pre-filled automatically** next time. Each entry picks a scope: **General** (true wherever you apply) / **Scenario** (tied to an applying channel) / **This time** (recorded but never auto-filled, for one-off values such as a referral code). Source and scope can be edited or removed in the Web form profile at any time, and **values the AI recognised are labeled “AI recognised”** because it is likelier than the rules to misread a field. **Custom Fields outside the catalogue** (a supervisor's name, a lab, say) can take part in Web form filling too: normal mode accepts only a unique exact match, and relaxed mode matches by label or context and flags low confidence; when something is ambiguous or fails a safety veto it does not guess, so proofread after filling. **There is exactly one destination, the Web form profile**: Resume fields are never learnt (the code that could modify them does not exist), and passwords, verification codes and other people's details are intercepted and cannot be learnt. Everything stays local and **is never read during Resume generation**|
